tasks.title: Create the Go CLI and dependency baseline
steps: Select and pin a supported Go version and the CLI exceptions listed in design.md. No database driver or hosted-service dependencies belong in Anza.
Create real version/help commands using flag.FlagSet and a run function returning an exit code. No cmd/anza-interview or second backend is created.
Use build variables for version/commit/build time without personal paths. Add formatting and lint configuration scoped to CLI packages.
acceptance: The CLI builds with an empty temporary HOME and no network at runtime.
Version/help report deterministic development defaults and perform no file writes; unknown flags return 2.
Module contains only CLI dependencies; there is no private chat module import or local replace directive.

tasks.title: Freeze shared schemas, fixtures and value types
steps: Materialize docs/contracts/v1.md revision 2 into Go value types and JSON schemas. Include existing chat camelCase envelopes plus the Anza snake_case domain payloads. Record fixtures and explicit field mapping in schema-decisions.md.

Implement strict new-domain decoding, duplicate-key rejection, canonical digests and useful field errors. Legacy chat response extension fields are tolerated only by the documented response decoder policy.

Create valid/invalid fixtures for each type, including Unicode, oversized data, unknown fields, integer overflow and recipe IDs. Test the planned camelCase wrapper and snake_case payload against contract fixtures. Read current chat fixtures read-only; document setup fields not yet present and defer source-backed parity to T3.6 TestAnzaContractFixture. Do not add chat-owned files from this Anza task.
acceptance: A changed plan operation changes its digest; map key order does not; duplicate keys are rejected.
Recommendation rejects command/url/path fields, unknown enums and oversized collections.

Every shared type round-trips canonical JSON; fixtures demonstrate required fields and limits. Current chat fixture gaps are documented, and T3.6 retains source-backed wrapper parity as an integration check.

tasks.title: Qualify vendor configuration and platform methods
steps: Read current official vendor install/auth/config docs and record source URL, retrieval date, supported CLI versions, platform prerequisites and exact method in vendor-methods.json.

Cover macOS arm64/amd64, native Windows amd64 and Linux Ubuntu 22.04/24.04 plus Debian 12 amd64/arm64 as proposed pilot targets. Classify other Windows ARM, WSL and musl combinations explicitly as qualified, manual or unsupported.

Distinguish subscription login, OpenRouter setup, model/tool-call support and config syntax. Use installed binaries only for read-only validation; defer new installs and paid requests to platform qualification.
Document privilege requirements, agent auto-update behavior, pinned version options and downloads that lack verifiable digest/signature. No invented artifact URLs or checksums.
acceptance: Each matrix cell names evidence and is marked documented_only until a real platform test exists.
Claude and Codex OpenRouter configuration have separate examples without tokens, auto-logout or permission bypass.
Each automated method states integrity verification and post-install detection; otherwise it remains manual.
test_cases: Validate every source record has method, platform, source URL, date and evidence level

tasks.title: Audit candidate skills and redistribution provenance
steps: Compare founder plan/apply/verify/review/journal/go workflows and selected ECC planning, verification and domain skills. Read supporting files and record dependencies instead of copying only SKILL.md.
For each candidate record source revision/path, purpose, license proof, attribution, personal assumptions, harness-specific tools, required scripts and keep/adapt/exclude decision.

Recommend small original portable anza-scope, anza-plan, anza-build, anza-check, anza-review, anza-continue skills; list domain additions separately. Flag unresolved rights instead of claiming every local file is redistributable.
acceptance: Every proposed bundled asset has verified permission or an original replacement task.
No home paths, private infrastructure references, customer data or credentials enter candidate exports.
Inventory differentiates shared instruction intent from agent-specific syntax and supporting tools.
test_cases: Review all selected rows for provenance and portable prerequisites

tasks.title: Build task and catalog metadata checks
steps: Implement a stdlib Python validator for execution-index.json, task docs, use-case coverage, dependency cycles and ownership using repository plus relative path; a chat path must not be interpreted as an Anza path.
Implement --compatibility and --content modes validating the metadata from T1.3/T1.4 when files exist; missing requested files must fail.
Return nonzero on malformed or absent evidence. The script validates artifacts, never edits plan status or certifies execution.
acceptance: Broken dependency, duplicate task, missing contract and overlapping concurrent output each fail with IDs.

The current planning artifact passes structural checks while preserving coordinator certification: T1.1 remains locally accepted and unexecuted tasks remain not_run; validation never rewrites certification.
Compatibility/content modes reject missing source dates and unclassified entries.
tasks.verification: python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts/tests -p test_check_plan.py; python3 scripts/check-plan.py

tasks.title: Inspect platforms and existing project tools read-only
steps: Implement OS/architecture/distro/shell detection and catalog-constrained executable/version probes with timeout and output bounds.
Inspect only selected project manifests after participant permission; do not execute project scripts or upload source. Detect symlinked roots and unsupported filesystems.
Produce reviewed MachineFacts without paths, usernames or a full installed-software inventory. Preserve absent/unknown/unsupported distinctions.
acceptance: Inspection writes nothing and never executes a project package script.
Missing executable, malformed version and timeout each produce distinct actionable results.
Darwin/Windows/Linux fixture facts map to declared compatibility cells; unsupported targets are explicit.

tasks.title: Implement private state, durable writes and locks
steps: Resolve OS/XDG state roots and stable canonical workspace identity; create owner-private directories and enforce Windows ACLs explicitly.
Implement lock acquisition in documented order, atomic replace and durable JSON journal persistence; inject filesystem faults in tests.
Keep lock owner PID/start identity and do not steal a live lock based on time alone. Detect malformed/newer schema state and preserve it.
acceptance: Second concurrent writer is rejected; process death permits a documented recovery path.
Interrupted write leaves either old or new valid data, never truncated state.
State permissions exclude other users; malformed/newer schema is not overwritten.

tasks.title: Implement bounded child process execution
steps: Run explicit executable/argument arrays without a shell by default; establish cwd and an allowlisted environment.
Implement cancellation of only the owned process tree on supported platforms, bounded captured output and deadline errors.
Represent sensitive environment values separately from serializable operation specs. Refuse unsafe relative executable resolution and redact logs.
acceptance: Arguments containing shell syntax remain literal in the child fixture.
Timeout/Ctrl-C ends child and owned descendants without killing an unrelated process.
Secrets and excessive output never enter serialized result or diagnostics.

tasks.title: Verify downloads and extract archives safely
steps: Implement HTTPS-only artifact fetches with expected digest, maximum size, deadline and constrained redirect hosts from trusted catalog data.
Validate archive entries before extraction: traversal, absolute paths, Windows drive/UNC paths, duplicate/case-fold targets, symlink/hardlink escape, device entries and decompression limits.
Download to private temporary storage, verify digest before executable permission and atomically install only after verification. Cache by digest.
acceptance: Wrong digest, oversized body, redirect to an unapproved host and archive escape fail before target writes.
A verified cached artifact can satisfy offline installation; unverified partial downloads cannot.
Participant/model input cannot override trusted expected checksum.

tasks.title: Implement OS credential storage and session-only fallback
steps: Use reviewed OS credential-store adapters with service name anza and credential IDs scoped to provider/workspace. Never place secrets in arguments, receipts or project config.
Provide masked terminal acquisition at the CLI seam and an in-memory session-only path if the store is unavailable; persist no plaintext fallback.
Delete only credentials recorded as created by Anza. Existing vendor credentials are outside ownership.
acceptance: Put/Get/Delete round-trip through a test adapter; unavailable keychain returns an explicit recoverable result.
No key value appears in JSON/debug/error output.
Removal of an Anza key never removes native Codex/Claude credentials.

tasks.title: Plan preserving JSON and TOML configuration edits
steps: Implement parse-and-patch edits for only supported managed keys/blocks. Preserve comments, unrelated keys and user formatting where possible; otherwise refuse with a manual diff.
Return planned bytes, preimage/postimage hashes and owned-key metadata without writing. Handle missing files separately from malformed existing files.
Define drift-aware inverse patches: undo Anza keys only if current values still match recorded postimage; preserve participant edits and unknown syntax.
acceptance: Existing comments and unrelated settings survive apply/reversal fixtures.
Duplicate keys, malformed syntax and user-owned conflicting keys produce a conflict without replacement.
Inverse patch never restores a whole stale backup over user changes.

tasks.title: Extend existing conversations for setup purpose and state
steps: Add optional immutable Conversation.Purpose and Setup state to the existing Conversation type. Empty purpose remains legacy intake. Reuse conversationID, transcriptStore and existing DynamoDB CAS/TTL/generation behavior; do not create a new session/token store.

Define setup protocol/catalog context, start request ID/body digest, setup status, recommendation/source version and privacy consent fields in setup_state.go. Native CLI generates the existing 64-hex random recovery token; server persists only its SHA256 ID. Define backend-local wire types in setup_types.go from the public protocol fixtures; do not import the Anza module just to get types.

Make existing store serialization and conversation deletion preserve/remove setup state with the whole conversation. Extend summary purpose metadata for the later mail/admin boundary task. Keep all existing fields and legacy JSON behavior.
Add strict setup creation validation using store.Put(previous=0), immutable purpose and body digest replay. A legacy intake token cannot silently become a setup conversation.
acceptance: Legacy conversation fixtures still round-trip unchanged while setup fields survive DynamoDB CAS and restart fixtures.
Matching start request replay returns the same setup state; changed body or intake-purpose token returns conflict.
GET/DELETE through the existing conversation lifecycle restores/removes setup state; missing/expired records follow existing visibility rules.

tasks.title: Add persistent setup-only admission to the shared backend
steps: Use the existing AWS SDK/client configuration to implement a setup coordination table adapter with DynamoDB conditional transactions for request state, per-conversation allowance and setup-wide daily cost reservations. Keep these rows out of the transcript table scanned by admin/mail.

Reuse the existing server allow/active ceilings as an additional shared per-instance limit. New persistent caps apply to setup calls; do not claim that unchanged intake calls have a new distributed hard cap.

Reserve conservative configured input/output/reasoning cost in integer micro-USD before calling the shared model client. Persist running/unknown/completed idempotency state; on ambiguous outcomes retain reservation and forbid automatic paid retry.

Implement explicit deletion/expiry cleanup that removes session-linking payloads while retaining only minimal non-content anti-replay/budget tombstones for their disclosed TTL. Costs/model prices/caps are configuration; missing required values disable setup only.
acceptance: Concurrent setup requests across simulated instances cannot exceed configured setup caps or duplicate a request ID.
A restart, timeout or day rollover preserves unresolved reservations and existing per-session allowances.
Missing quota configuration rejects setup calls without breaking ordinary website intake; transcript scans never encounter quota rows.

tasks.title: Extract and reuse the existing model transport
steps: Extract the raw request/response portion of answerWithPrompt into one reusable server method in model.go. Keep answer/answerWithPrompt as compatibility wrappers that preserve citation filtering, title token limits, selected endpoint/key and provider-specific parameters.

Return raw text and optional usage metadata for structured setup output before citation filtering. Reuse s.client, s.key, s.model, s.endpoint and loadRuntimeCredentials; no new provider secret or independent provider router.

Apply bounded output/deadline/error classification to the shared helper. Do not switch the existing configured provider, enable fallback or alter the existing contact-intake prompt changes; integrate only from the reconciled peer baseline.

Add HTTP transport fixtures asserting both legacy payloads and setup JSON behavior, including malformed/truncated responses and absent usage. Missing usage keeps a full conservative setup reservation.
acceptance: Existing ask/title/brief/Experiential fixtures retain their request parameters, citation output and failure semantics.
Setup generation uses the same model endpoint/client/credential as intake and receives unfiltered structured output plus usage when available.
No additional provider client, credential store or network retry loop is introduced.

tasks.title: Add a setup interview policy and typed recommendations
steps: Create setupService as a consumer of the existing server/store/shared model helper, shared turn policy, and setup quota adapter. Keep the general intake prompt, booking and brief behavior intact; use a setup-specific prompt only for immutable setup-purpose conversations.

Use reviewed brief/machine facts as context in the existing bounded server-held history. Ask only missing setup questions through /api/ask; answers remain the existing AskResponse shape. Recommendation generation is a separate explicit setup action.

Embed only reviewed recommendation metadata from the sealed Anza catalog. Copy public wire fixtures with version/digest provenance into chat testdata; do not import the Anza executable or runtime-fetch a participant-provided catalog URL.

Generate typed Recommendation via the shared raw model helper, validate catalog IDs/platform constraints and persist exact source version/context digest. Manual steps remain plain text. Bound repair to one charged attempt under the same quota.

Unknown network outcome and stale versions invalidate generation safely; new setup messages/context edits invalidate older recommendations. Setup cannot book, approve a learner brief or invent a workshop agenda.
acceptance: A reviewed project brief avoids repeated project-goal questions while setup-specific missing facts are still requested.
Prompt injection, unknown recipe IDs and stale/catalog-mismatched recommendations never become executable local operations.
The setup flow calls the existing model transport and conversation lifecycle; no duplicate interview server or storage engine is created.

tasks.title: Implement additive setup handlers alongside existing chat routes
steps: Implement capability/session/context/recommendation handlers per contract v1 revision 2 on setupService, reusing transcriptHeaders, conversationID, writeJSON and transcriptStore. Do not register new routes or edit the main router until T3.6.

Use the same X-Conversation-Token and stable requestId semantics as chat. Start accepts reviewed setup facts; new tokens are participant-generated. No invitation or independent bearer-session protocol.
Test real HTTP requests through a local handler mux for every documented method/status/body, origin policy, feature flag, session-purpose isolation and strict new payload size/field limits.
Require completed current setup turn and exact version for recommendation. Ordinary conversation GET/DELETE remain the sole resume/deletion endpoints.
acceptance: All new setup handler success and negative statuses are covered at the real HTTP boundary.
A website intake token cannot request setup-only mutations and setup tokens cannot mutate booking or learner-brief state.
CLI requests without Origin work as existing chat permits; browser CORS is not broadened.

tasks.title: Wire setup mode into the existing server and preserve legacy routes
steps: Add optional setup service field/initialization to existing server and register only additive setup routes. In /api/ask, dispatch existing setup-purpose conversations through setupService while retaining the legacy branch and response format.

Default ANZA_SETUP_ENABLED to false. A missing/invalid setup-only configuration disables setup capability and its routes with a clear status; existing health/intake/title/brief/booking still function.

Reuse provider secrets, shared HTTP process, storage and graceful shutdown. Apply quota/mode guards before provider calls; use shared allow/active exactly once per call. Do not introduce a new executable or health service.

Provide an opt-in loopback setup test fixture using the real shared router and fake storage/provider. Its startup writes a temporary ready file; no live credentials/model/calendar calls. This supports the Anza cross-repo CLI acceptance task.
Document additive API/config and gate rollout on existing website contact/intake/title/brief/booking regression results from the reconciled peer baseline.
acceptance: Feature disabled preserves all existing route behavior and the current contact-intake prompt tests.
Feature enabled runs both website intake and Anza setup through the same server/store/model client with purpose isolation.
Missing setup quota/catalog configuration does not cause shared server startup failure or an unrelated website outage.

tasks.title: Reuse turn reservation with a setup-specific replay policy
steps: Extract shared reservation/completion mechanics from reserveTurn/finishTurn into policy-aware helpers; retain legacy wrappers and exact legacy behavior.

For setup turns enforce existing requestId/body identity, expected conversation version, setup limit and durable quota request state. An expired lease after an ambiguous provider call is not permission to generate again.
Invalidate setup recommendations when source turns or context change; keep learner-brief invalidation behavior unchanged for intake. Resolve server-owned full history exactly once.
Test completed replay, in-flight request, failed-before-send, unknown-after-send and conflicting concurrent turns without changing website retry semantics.
acceptance: Both intake and setup use shared turn persistence/CAS code; legacy retry tests remain green.
A setup request with unknown provider outcome cannot create a second paid call by waiting for lease expiry.
New setup content makes previously generated recommendations stale without silently altering a learner brief.

tasks.title: Protect shared admin, mail and deletion boundaries
steps: Default setup-purpose conversations out of scheduled owner transcript email. Teach the existing mail reader to skip explicit purpose=setup while treating absent purpose as existing intake; preserve existing mail dedup/booking behavior.
Keep legacy owner lists backward compatible; expose setup summaries only through an explicit owner-authorized purpose filter. Never serve setup context through unauthenticated admin output.

Ensure shared conversation DELETE/expiry also invokes setup coordination cleanup through an optional hook without importing installer concerns. Minimal budget tombstones remain content-free with documented TTL. Add an optional server cleanup callback field with nil preserving legacy behavior; T3.6 wires it when setup is enabled. This task owns that narrow main.go field addition after the transport refactor.

Document actual shared retention: configured AWS transcript TTL, separate provider capture policy, setup mail exclusion and deletion limits. Do not promise 24-hour retention or inherit email consent silently.
acceptance: Existing intake mail fixtures behave unchanged and setup records trigger no SES send.
Owner and participant isolation tests cover both conversation purposes without leaking setup facts.
Deletion removes active setup content while retaining only disclosed minimal quota/replay metadata; no claimed deletion of provider copies.
tasks.verification: go test . -run "TestSetupPrivacy|TestSetupAdmin|TestAdmin|TestConversation" -count=1; go vet .; python3 -m unittest discover -s infra/lambda -p "test_*.py"

tasks.title: Implement Anza client for the existing chat protocol
steps: Use the shared Sanifu base URL and X-Conversation-Token protocol. Generate 32 random bytes as 64 lowercase hex characters, save only in private local state and keep it out of URLs/logs.

Call additive setup capability/start/context/recommendation endpoints, /api/ask for questions, and /api/conversation for resume/delete per contract revision 2. Do not parse an installation plan from free-text answers.
Persist stable requestId and expected versions; on network timeout read conversation state before retrying. Distinguish legacy AskResponse from typed setup recommendation and verify catalog digest.
Handle disabled feature, unsupported catalog, 409/429/503 and expired/missing state with useful guidance; no new session service, invitation token or model fallback.
acceptance: Client fixtures match the existing chat camelCase request/response and recovery-token rules exactly.
Resume reuses request identity and resolves shared conversation state; ambiguous generation is not automatically repeated.
Only reviewed project facts go to chat; participant agent credentials and raw repository files never do.

tasks.title: Import and review an optional learner brief
steps: Read a learner-selected bounded ProjectBrief JSON or approved learner-brief text export. Existing chat LearnerBrief.Text is plain text, so do not pretend it already supplies typed project fields.
Preview the imported content before upload. A typed brief uses the structured schema; a text export is sent as clearly labeled untrusted context and the setup interview confirms missing facts.
Never read browser localStorage, a browser recovery token or a private transcript automatically. A future direct browser-to-CLI handoff needs separate explicit authorization/design.
acceptance: A valid typed brief or learner-reviewed text export carries project context without inventing structured facts or an agenda.
Credential/contact/transcript token fields in typed imports fail without logging their values.
Import preserves source files and performs no network call before participant review.

tasks.title: Implement accessible interview wizard
steps: Build line-oriented prompts with injectable input/output; one question at a time, plain language, beginner/developer explanation levels and skip/back/resume.
Preview facts/brief upload and the existing shared backend privacy disclosure before generating a private recovery token and starting setup. No invitation code or duplicate sign-up is needed.
Use server context updates for back/edit and invalidate recommendation approval when facts change. Detect non-TTY/EOF, suppress ANSI and save private progress; no tool installation occurs here.
acceptance: Scripted beginner/developer sessions reach a typed recommendation through the shared chat protocol.
EOF/Ctrl-C saves/respects contract exit states and never records consent silently.
Plain terminal output needs no color/cursor control and never displays the recovery token.

tasks.title: Implement exact-plan review and digest approval
steps: Render plan tools, purpose, versions, downloads, privilege, costs/account owner, config diff, manual steps and reversal limits in plain text and JSON.
Prompt for explicit approval and store Approval bound to the canonical digest. Display refusal, editing and expired-plan paths.
Implement noninteractive --approve-digest validation only; --yes or profile selection cannot stand in for exact approval.
acceptance: Any plan edit/expiry invalidates prior approval.
JSON stdout is parseable and diagnostic prose stays on stderr.
Participant can decline without installations/config writes.

tasks.title: Load and validate versioned recipe and pack catalog
steps: Implement catalog loading from an injected fs.FS, checksums, unique IDs, supported platform predicates and dependency cycle validation. Test with real temporary catalog fixtures; production embedding is T5.7.

Validate recipe and pack entries against their v1 schemas and provenance; references must resolve. v1 defines no Exercise type/schema, so reject exercise entries explicitly and defer that content until a versioned schema is authored. Missing optional domain recipes remain unsupported until added.
Expose read-only catalog interfaces for server/planner without runtime network fetch. Produce initial manifest metadata; T5.7 seals its inventory after content workers finish.
acceptance: Unknown recipe, digest mismatch, cycle and missing license/source are rejected.
Same release yields the same catalog digest across OS builds.
Partial catalog never claims tools exist if their executable recipe is absent.

tasks.title: Author portable common teaching skills
steps: Author six concise original/adapted workflows for real projects using content-inventory decisions; include useful-slice acceptance and continuation notes.
Separate instructions from optional scripts; remove founder paths, fleet infrastructure, model names, unavailable tool calls and obligatory external actions.
Record per-asset attribution/license/adaptation and ensure beginner wording explains verification. Same workflow intent must work in both agents.
acceptance: Each skill names trigger, inputs, concrete outputs and how the participant checks completion.
No skill silently publishes, spends, reads secrets or requires a private tool.
Pack resolves all asset hashes/provenance and passes catalog validation.
test_cases: TestCatalogValidation against core pack; human review of six workflows using a sample real project

tasks.title: Define base agent and Git installation recipes
steps: Encode qualified Codex, Claude Code and Git methods per supported platform from compatibility evidence, with exact detection/verification and privilege disclosures.
Prefer verified per-user artifact installation where available; vendor scripts/package-manager methods must disclose bootstrap trust and remain explicitly reviewed.
Set existing installations to preserve/use if compatible; require a separate reviewed upgrade when incompatible. Mark SDK/license/OS-owned dependencies manual.
acceptance: Both agents are selected by the base profile; install detection prevents duplicate installations.
Every automated target has real source/version/integrity data or a documented vendor trust method; placeholders fail validation.
Git installation cannot run a privileged command without a distinct prompt.

tasks.title: Define web and automation toolchain packs
steps: Define Node-based web and optional browser-automation capabilities with pinned qualified tool methods and explicit download sizes/licenses.
Keep editor, GitHub CLI and browser tooling optional; select by project facts, not all-at-once defaults.
Define a non-destructive new scratch project or read-only existing-project check; package scripts require preview and separate execution consent.
acceptance: Web needs select only prerequisites and relevant skills; no unnecessary paid hosting provisioning.
Existing project source is not overwritten by an exercise.
Unavailable browser/system requirements return manual actions rather than ready.

tasks.title: Define Python, data/ML and Go packs
steps: Define per-project Python environments and Go tooling with qualified methods; preserve existing interpreter/module versions.
Separate CPU readiness from optional GPU/CUDA/remote-compute requirements. Zerfoo is optional where fit is established, never a universal ML requirement.
Provide exercises that check local imports/build/run on a scratch example or participant-approved existing commands, without downloading customer datasets.
acceptance: Existing Python/Go projects retain declared versions and lockfiles.
GPU-required project on CPU machine reports unmet requirement explicitly.
No cloud/GPU allocation or model training charges occur during setup.

tasks.title: Define mobile, desktop and unsupported-domain paths
steps: Encode platform prerequisites for iOS, Android and desktop projects, distinguishing automatically installable components from manual SDK/store/license/device steps.
For any unmodeled domain preserve project goal and return a useful manual recommendation with missing capability IDs; never narrow the interview to only shipped packs.
Record architecture/storage/reboot constraints for SDKs and prohibit automatic license acceptance or device provisioning.
acceptance: iOS on Windows/Linux produces a macOS requirement, not a fake successful install.
Android/desktop setup shows manual SDK/license steps where qualification is absent.
Unknown stack can finish interview with partial readiness and actionable guidance.

tasks.title: Seal and embed the complete reviewed content catalog
steps: Implement root catalog package embedding the named data directories; internal/catalog loads that embedded filesystem. Do not attempt a go:embed path containing parent-directory traversal.
Generate a sorted manifest of content files/digests/provenance references and catalog version from reviewed assets. Exclude Go files and local state; generator --check is read-only.
Run complete reference/recipe/license/platform validation against bundled content and freeze a digest for service/CLI interoperability.

Generate a sanitized setup recommendation catalog artifact containing IDs, purposes, platform constraints and content version/digest only. The chat contract owner copies/pins it at build time; no executable commands/download URLs or private module dependency cross that boundary.
acceptance: Production CLI/service use the same immutable bundled catalog digest.
Missing asset, stale manifest, duplicate ID, unlicensed content or unknown dependency fails qualification.
Regeneration is deterministic and contains no machine-specific paths.
tasks.verification: python3 scripts/catalog-manifest.py --check; go test ./internal/catalog -count=1; go vet ./internal/catalog

tasks.title: Build deterministic local installation plans
steps: Resolve validated recipe/pack IDs and pure agent adapter outputs into dependency-ordered operations using actual machine/project facts and existing state. Compute approval digest only after both adapters have contributed all configuration changes.
Reject cycles, unsupported targets, escaping logical destinations, unknown privileges and data-derived commands. Preserve compatible installed tools and existing user files.
Calculate preimage/postimage digests, warnings/manual steps and expiry with injected clock/ID; output identical plans for identical inputs.
acceptance: Changing machine facts/catalog/preimages changes approval digest.
Unsupported capabilities become explicit manual constraints and cannot enter executable operations.
Repeat planning on an already completed setup yields no duplicate install/config writes.

tasks.title: Implement Codex configuration adapter
steps: Produce config patches and managed skill copy operations for the qualified Codex versions using compatibility.md.
Support native subscription mode and named OpenRouter selection without defaulting global provider changes; provider key reference is symbolic only.
Preserve existing AGENTS.md, config tables, trust settings, hooks and skills. Conflicts and unsupported versions return explicit results.
acceptance: Fixtures preserve unrelated TOML/comments and global instructions.
No permission bypass, auto-trust or subscription token export appears in generated config.
OpenRouter adapter contains no secret and maps to the qualified provider syntax.

tasks.title: Implement Claude Code configuration adapter
steps: Produce supported Claude project configuration/skills and provider launch environment descriptors from qualified compatibility data.
Handle shared/symlinked skill directories and existing CLAUDE.md/settings without replacing them; ensure one managed copy per real target.
Detect subscription/OpenRouter conflict and explain participant action instead of deleting cached auth. Leave permission mode and hooks untouched unless explicitly selected.
acceptance: Existing settings and global instruction files survive; malformed settings are refused.
OpenRouter variables are injected at launch with explicit conflicting-key handling, never secret config values.
Duplicate discovery roots do not create conflicting skill copies.

tasks.title: Execute approved operations with receipts and crash recovery
steps: Apply only matching fresh digest under state locks; adapters have already contributed operations in the reviewed plan. Never add operations after approval. Recheck preimages immediately before each effect.
Implement typed copy/config/download/vendor/package operations through injected filesystem/process boundaries. Journal intent, effect result and ownership with durable receipts.
On crash reconcile each running operation by postcondition; unknown package effects remain manual. Roll back only unchanged Anza-owned file/key edits; privilege denial returns resumable state.
acceptance: Stale approval or changed preimage produces zero new writes.
Fault injection before/after each operation yields recoverable valid state and never duplicates a proven successful install.
Unowned file/symlink appearing after planning is preserved and yields conflict.

tasks.title: Launch both agents with independent access choices
steps: Resolve provider per agent/workspace, acquire OpenRouter key from OS store/session env, and inject only into the owned child environment.
Guide native subscription login using vendor-supported interactive commands; do not ingest or forward native tokens. Handle cancellations without claiming authenticated.
Implement anza run argument forwarding and explain difference from ordinary vendor launches; no shell aliases or profiles containing secrets.
acceptance: Mixed subscription/OpenRouter choices launch distinct correct child environments.
Secrets are absent from argv/logs/receipts; parent/global environment is unchanged.
Missing credentials or vendor conflict returns actionable instructions without automatic logout.

tasks.title: Report local and paid readiness separately
steps: Check installed executable versions, config validity, selected skills, account availability and unresolved platform/manual steps per required capability.
Keep default checks local. Implement optional tiny live agent check only after separate cost/account disclosure and participant confirmation; enforce timeout and record real evidence.
Aggregate mandatory statuses conservatively; skipped live checks remain unverified and never imply account entitlement or model success.
acceptance: Installed-but-unauthenticated is action_required; local-ready-but-no-live-evidence is clearly distinguished.
Denied live confirmation causes zero provider/agent requests.
Unsupported mandatory platform requirement prevents overall ready status.

tasks.title: Run a project-specific first verification exercise
steps: Resolve a reviewed catalog exercise by project needs; show commands and expected output before execution.
For new projects use a dedicated Anza-owned scratch directory; for existing projects default to read-only checks and ask separately before package scripts or writes.
Return observed outcome, limitations and next-step instructions. Never claim completion of a customer feature from a toolchain exercise.
acceptance: A selected exercise produces real recorded output or an explicit unmet prerequisite.
Existing participant files are unchanged by default.
Failure/cancellation preserves useful diagnostics without customer/source upload.

tasks.title: Implement catalog and binary update planning
steps: Fetch verified release metadata under explicit check/update commands; no background auto-update daemon.
Compare installed catalog/binary versions and produce a new reviewed plan with compatibility changes and migration effects.
Keep prior verified binary/receipt until the new executable passes local version check; refuse downgrade/replay without explicit selection and supported migration.
acceptance: Update check makes no configuration or binary changes.
Bad signature/digest or incompatible state leaves old installation usable.
User-edited managed content yields conflict, not forced replacement.

tasks.title: Implement ownership-limited uninstall and repair
steps: Preview receipt-owned removals and inverse patches; preserve participant edits and external/preexisting tools.
Remove only matching Anza-created files/keys after explicit confirmation, retain unresolved conflicts and disclose system packages left installed.
Repair re-detects real state and creates a new reviewed plan; never replays old approvals or blindly reinstalls unknown operations.
acceptance: Uninstall preserves every unowned or modified fixture path and native login credential.
Partially removed state remains valid and a second removal is idempotent.
Repair cannot overwrite drift or claim a failed action succeeded.

tasks.title: Create opt-in redacted diagnostics and local deletion
steps: Export only allowlisted version/platform/status/operation metadata; no automatic upload, interview text, raw config, paths or environment.
Preview destination/content summary; use private permissions and redact unexpected secrets in errors as defense in depth.

Delete local setup session state and use existing chat DELETE /api/conversation with its recovery token for server deletion. Report shared AWS TTL, provider-copy limits and minimal anti-replay retention honestly.
acceptance: Seeded secrets in all error/config fixtures never appear in diagnostics.
Export requires explicit output request and performs no network upload.
Local delete cannot remove project source, unrelated state or vendor auth.

tasks.title: Wire the full CLI command graph
steps: Wire every CLI command in v1 to real package implementations, with injected stdio/context and documented exit codes.
Make default wizard interview -> plan -> review -> apply -> login guidance -> doctor -> exercise, with truthful partial readiness on user skip.
Verify noninteractive operation refuses missing consent/credentials instead of hanging; ensure help/version stay side-effect-free.

tasks.title: Implement POSIX one-line bootstrap
steps: Implement sh-compatible OS/architecture detection and HTTPS download using a versioned installer with an embedded expected release-manifest SHA256. Verify manifest hash, then artifact hash, using supported native SHA256 tools. The HTTPS-delivered installer is the initial trust root; do not claim independent signature verification in shell.
Install into per-user bin without requiring Go/Node/admin; preserve an existing incompatible binary until explicit update. Explain PATH and support version override.
Use /dev/tty only when available for wizard input after piped bootstrap; noninteractive mode downloads/prints next step without hanging or reading script stdin.
acceptance: POSIX fixtures cover macOS/Linux architectures, unsupported target, missing fetch/hash tool, bad manifest/artifact digest, interrupted download and paths with spaces.
Bootstrap cannot execute an unverified download or overwrite an unowned binary.
Interactive successful bootstrap invokes installed Anza once; noninteractive invocation does not wait.

tasks.title: Implement native PowerShell bootstrap
steps: Implement Windows architecture/version detection and release download using a versioned installer with an embedded expected manifest SHA256; verify manifest and artifact with native cryptographic hashing.
Use per-user bin and atomic replacement with executable-in-use handling; update only user PATH after disclosure and preserve unrelated PATH entries.
Handle constrained execution policy/admin absence with actionable instructions; never disable policy globally or require WSL silently.
acceptance: Windows fixtures cover spaces/non-ASCII home, locked binary, unsupported arch, corrupt manifest/artifact and cancelled download.
No admin or Go compiler is required for supported bootstrap.
Policy restriction returns guidance without modifying machine security settings.

steps: Build explicit GOOS/GOARCH artifacts for qualified matrix using pinned Go/deps, trimpath and version metadata. Produce SBOM/licenses/checksums and Ed25519-signed release metadata for CLI updates; stamp manifest SHA256 into versioned bootstrap scripts after artifact build.
Run targeted tests, whole-module integration and go vet/lint on required native runners; missing native runner means unqualified, not pass.
Prepare manual gated release workflow with minimal permissions and no publish on ordinary PRs; include rollback/revocation/compromised-release procedure.

Release only the Anza CLI and content artifacts from this repository. Shared backend image/config is built and deployed through chat existing infrastructure; coordinate advertised catalog compatibility and deploy the additive backend first.
Payload manifest covers binaries/content only. Generate bootstrap scripts afterward with its digest; do not recursively include those scripts in that same manifest. Record script hashes separately.
acceptance: CI rejects missing tests, failed native jobs, changed generated schemas and integrity failures.

Every artifact has exact platform/name/version/digest. Both bootstraps pin manifest hashes; the Go updater verifies Ed25519 signatures using an embedded public key. Document initial HTTPS trust and signing-key rotation/revocation.
No production release is created by this preparation task.
